t: You're looking at the Athenaeum Club, a Grade I listed building and a private members' club, founded in 1824. It's meant for people with intellectual interests, especially those distinguished in science, engineering, literature or the arts. Humphry Davy and Michael Faraday were its first chairman and secretary, and fifty-one Nobel Laureates have been members. Decimus Burton, an early member, designed the clubhouse, and his father's company built it. Thomas Lawrence and John Wilson Croker are both counted among its founders. Lawrence was a celebrated portrait painter, and Croker was first secretary to the Admiralty.
